model_annotation: This plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC) of several methods as a function of co-occurrence number. The x-axis represents "Co-occurrence Number" on a logarithmic scale, ranging from approximately 3 to about 5,000, with tick marks at 5, 10¹, 10², 10³, and beyond. The y-axis represents "ACC (%)" on a linear scale, ranging from approximately 38% to 66%, with tick marks at intervals of 5 percentage points. Six lines are shown, each corresponding to a different method. The "Base" line (black, solid, with circle markers) starts at approximately 38% at the lowest co-occurrence number and rises slightly to around 43.5% at the highest, showing a relatively flat trend. The "FT" line (blue, solid, with downward-triangle markers) begins near 40% and increases to approximately 47.5%. The "IKE" line (red, solid, with upward-triangle markers) starts at roughly 43% and rises to about 49% at the highest co-occurrence number. The "MEND" line (brown, solid, with diamond markers) begins at approximately 44.5% and increases to around 56.5%, showing a steady upward trend. The "MEMIT" line (purple, solid, with pentagon markers) starts near 44% and rises to approximately 54.5%, with a noticeable increase between the third and fourth data points. The "ROME" line (green, solid, with square markers) starts at approximately 51% at the lowest co-occurrence number and climbs to roughly 66% at the highest, exhibiting the steepest overall increase among all methods. All lines generally trend upward with increasing co-occurrence number, though at varying rates and with different starting values.
